root_idea.summary: The root centers on cutting or splitting something lengthwise, especially into an elongated form.
root_idea.development: From lengthwise cutting, the usage extends to strips and thongs, bodily shape and proportion, division into distinct parties or ways, and figurative acts of distinguishing or arranging affairs.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form I verb; the inflected QAC identity is normalized to the classical perfect citation form قَدَّ.
Quran-attested plural adjective/noun form, presented under the supported singular lexical citation form قِدَّة.

senses.definition: To cut or tear something lengthwise, splitting it along its length.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic passage about a shirt, the verb occurs actively as قَدَّتْ and passively as قُدَّ; the construction specifies whether the tear is from the front or from the back.

senses.definition: Diverse or divided into distinct ways, parties, or sects.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the plural قِدَدًا in the expression طَرَائِقَ قِدَدًا; it describes ways or groups that are separate and differing from one another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut something off completely, or to cut it without specifying a direction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical usage alongside the more specific lengthwise-cutting sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cross or cut through a desert or the night by traveling through it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative extension of cutting through a space or period.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a road to cut someone off from companions or from the object of a journey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional construction with the road as the subject or cause of separation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut short or break off speech; in another reported usage, to articulate speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source reports more than one interpretation of this construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut out or shape something in any manner; figuratively, to make someone well-shaped or beautiful in proportion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The figurative use concerns conformation or proportion rather than the act of cutting itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suffer a cutting pain in the belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized bodily usage associated with قُدَاد.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make dried meat by cutting flesh into strips or elongated pieces and drying it, with or without salting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The derived Form II verb describes the preparation of قَدِيد.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a garment to fit or suit someone in size and length.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of clothing in relation to the person wearing it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For food to cause abdominal pain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form IV construction with food as the subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a garment or piece of cloth to become extensively slit, torn, ragged, or worn out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of cloth that has deteriorated through repeated tearing or wear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For flesh-meat to become cut into strips and dried.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A quasi-passive usage corresponding to the preparation of dried meat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a company of people to become separated into distinct parties.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The separation is expressed through becoming قِدَد, or separate groups.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a thing to become dry or dry up.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general intransitive usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a she-camel to change in condition from fat to lean, or from lean to fat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source reports both directions of change according to different authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a skin, garment, or similar article to become cut, split, or torn lengthwise, or to be cut off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is specifically associated with items such as skins, clothing, bags, and related articles.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To consider and arrange affairs, forecasting their outcomes and distinguishing between them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form VIII usage concerning deliberation and management.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To continue uniformly or in one consistent state or course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of an affair or of camels proceeding undeviatingly along one course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sufficiency; enough or what is sufficient.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun used indeclinably, synonymous with حَسْبُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suffice or be enough for someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal-noun usage equivalent to يَكْفِي, as in قَدْنِي, “it suffices me.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Expectation or anticipation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A particle used with a verb, especially with a future or imperfect verb in contexts of anticipated occurrence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The nearness of a past event to the present, often rendered “just” or “already.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A particle used with a past verb; the source also discusses its use in circumstantial clauses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rarity or paucity of an occurrence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported particle usage whose interpretation may overlap with affirmation or with rarity inferred from the surrounding statement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Frequency or repeated occurrence, sometimes equivalent to رُبَّمَا.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A particle usage attested in non-Quranic literary examples.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Affirmation of truth, certainty, or indeed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a verb, especially before a past verb in emphatic assertions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Negation, in a rare reported construction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An unusual usage in which the particle is said to occupy the place of مَا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The skin of a lamb or kid, especially a small skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may also occur in proverbial expressions contrasting a small skin or affair with a larger hide or matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: What makes a small or inferior matter comparable to a great or noble one?
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proverbial expression applied to someone who exceeds the proper limit or compares the contemptible with the noble.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The size, measure, bulk, bodily figure, stature, or proportion of a thing or person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes equality in size and beauty or symmetry of bodily form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of marine fish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized lexical item; it is traditionally said to increase sexual vigor when eaten.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing cut lengthwise or in an elongated form.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes something characterized by the result of قَدَّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thong cut from untanned skin, used for sewing footwear, binding captives, or fastening saddles and similar equipment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may be a single thong or a collective term for such thongs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A whip.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported lexical use, also interpreted in one cited expression as referring to another meaning of قِدّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sandal cut lengthwise from skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may also refer specifically to a sandal retaining its hair for pliability.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vessel made of skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It can be contrasted with a vessel made of wood or with a fragment of a drinking vessel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression شَدِيدُ القِدِّ, either a strong bowstring or strength in drawing a bow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source reports an interpretive variation in this traditional expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece or portion of a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The basic nominal sense is extended to a distinct portion or division.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hedgehog or a jerboa.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical item is reported with both animal identifications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pain in the belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It also occurs in an imprecation wishing this pain upon someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Meat cut into strips or elongated pieces and dried, often after salting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form is a passive-result noun for prepared dried meat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A garment or piece of cloth that is slit or torn and old and worn out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive use for deteriorated cloth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small garment or mat of coarse hair-cloth worn by people of low condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A diminutive term carrying an association with humble or low status.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The followers or camp followers of an army, including itinerant craftsmen such as farriers and blacksmiths.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal or specialized collective term; variant pronunciations are reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel long in the back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source itself reports that this word may instead derive from قَوْد.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A road or route.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative formation understood as a way that has been cut or opened.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The external female genital opening.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The part of the back of the neck between the ears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source treats this as a dialectal variant of, or possible error for, مَقَذٌّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An even or level plain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized geographical usage synonymous with قَاعٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An iron instrument used for cutting skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tool noun derived from the act of cutting skin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wine associated with al-Maqadd, or wine boiled down until reduced to half its original quantity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source reports both a geographical designation and an explanation based on division into halves; pronunciation variants occur.

cautions: The Quranic verb group is attested in inflected active and passive forms; the public headword is normalized to the Form I perfect citation form قَدَّ.
Lane also records قَدْ as a grammatical particle and noun; these uses are kept separate from the lexical cutting branches.
The expression شَدِيدُ القِدِّ has a reported ambiguity between a strong bowstring and strength in drawing a bow.
The entry قَيْدُودٌ is included because it occurs in the supplied Lane primary material, although that source itself suggests derivation from قَوْد.
